title: Serving runtime incident playbook — eviction/deadlock exploration
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for on-call and post-incident work when the serving runtime shows signs of memory pressure, KV cache corruption, or a mutex-related deadlock that manifests as throughput stall. The doc is intentionally pragmatic — fast triage steps, short-lived mitigations, and a checklist for deeper postmortem and engineering fixes.

Context / why we need it:
- Recent trend: intermittent stalls where a small fraction (~0.5–1%) of pods go to near-zero QPS for 30–120s then recover. Symptoms: slow token generation, suddenly high per-request latency, and increased retry spikes.
- Observed root causes in past incidents: a) heap fragmentation under mixed sized embeddings allocations; b) KV index desync after race during eviction; c) continuous-batching scheduler entering priority inversion and holding locks.

Quick detection heuristics (alert runbook):
1) Check latency spike and QPS drop windows in Grafana — correlate to node/pod level.
2) Look for OOMKill events (kube events) or repeated GC thrash in logs.
3) Search runtime logs for repeated "eviction failed" / "index mismatch" / "batcher stuck waiting" messages.
4) If GPU workloads: nvidia-smi shows process with high memory but low utilization.
5) If CPU-only: top/pmap to confirm resident set sizes.

Immediate on-call triage (first 10–20m):
- Goal: get customers back online with minimal risk; preserve evidence for postmortem.

A) Surface-level checks (non-disruptive):
- kubectl get pods -n redwood-serving | grep -E "CrashLoopBackOff|OOMKilled|Evicted"
- kubectl describe pod <pod> for events; save output.
- kubectl exec -it <pod> -- pmap 1 | head -n 40  (ps/pmap summary)
- kubectl exec -it <pod> -- cat /proc/<pid>/status | egrep "VmRSS|VmPeak|Threads"
- Export logs for the window: logging query for pod, time range, save to artifact store.

B) If the pod is responsive but slow: collect live diagnostics (non-killing):
- thread dumps: kubectl exec -it <pod> -- kill -SIGUSR1 1  (service prints stacks to its log; confirm which signal is safe)
- heap snapshot (if supported): trigger internal endpoint /debug/heap or use jemalloc stats if built with MALLOC_CONF; capture to artifacts.
- batcher metrics: check /metrics endpoint for continuous_batching_active, queue_length, oldest_request_age.

C) If pod is unresponsive and not OOMKilled: avoid immediate restart unless necessary to restore traffic. Prefer draining and warm replacement steps below.

Short-term mitigation (get traffic moving):
- Scale up healthy pods (avoid adding identical version if suspect regression).
- Use rollout fallback: route traffic to previous stable model runtime variant or reduce concurrency (set concurrency limit for the pod/container to 1 or small value).
- Disable continuous batching on a per-deployment basis: patch deployment with env var CONTINUOUS_BATCHING=false and apply as a canary to a couple nodes first.
- Force graceful drain for afflicted nodes: kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data <node> then cordon the node. This forces workloads to rehydrate on other nodes (may clear local KV state).

Safe restart cadence (if chosen):
- For suspected KV-cache corruption: restart sequence must be ordered to avoid cascade corruption — restart a single pod, verify it rejoins healthy and serves, then progressively restart the rest. Do NOT mass restart unless under load blackout and agreed in channel.
- If OOMKills prevalent: reduce configured max batch size and token budget env vars in a canary, verify effect, then rollout.

KV cache integrity checks (diagnostics):
- Run checksum script: /opt/serving/bin/kvcache-checksum --snapshot /var/lib/serving/kvcache --verify-index; capture output.
- Look for suspicious logs like "index header checksum mismatch" or "put with nonexistent key id".
- If index mismatch present, prefer controlled rebuild: set env VAR KVCACHE_REBUILD_ON_START=true and restart single instance; monitor memory usage and rebuild time.

Deadlock investigation (fast path):
- Collect multiple thread dumps (3 x 10s apart) to see stable stacks holding locks.
- Use pstack / gdb -p <pid> to capture backtraces; save to artifact.
- Identify mutex names or symbols from stack traces. Map to code: grep in repo for symbol names to find lock owners.
- If lock held by background compaction/eviction thread, consider disabling compaction or switching compaction to low-priority thread pool.
- Quick mitigation: flip feature flag to degrade to single-threaded eviction or to avoid certain code paths (feature flags: kvcache_compaction_enabled=false, batcher_priority_scaling=false).

Batching regressions (what to look for):
- Metrics: continuous_batching_latency, average_batch_size, empty_batch_rate. A regression often shows a drop in avg batch size plus increase in latency and queue waiting time.
- Triage: set max_batch_wait_ms lower, set per-route batching_threshold higher (reduce pooling).
- If scheduler spin detected: kill and restart batcher thread via admin endpoint rather than full process (if admin supports hot-swap).

Evidence preservation checklist (do this before destructive ops):
- Save pod logs (kubectl logs > file).
- Save thread dumps and heap snapshots.
- Save current /metrics output.
- Record exact kubectl/hpa deployment revisions and environment variables.
- Archive node dmesg and kernel OOM logs.

Post-incident immediate tasks (within 24–72h):
- Create incident ticket with timeline and attach artifacts.
- Engineering: reproduce in a staging environment using a traffic pattern replay (capture requests and re-run against patched images).
- Product/SRE: evaluate customer impact and timeline for a postmortem doc and remediation plan.

Longer-term engineering fixes (candidates):
- Add CRC checks on KV index updates and stronger write-atomicity (two-phase commit for index header).
- Introduce watchdog for batcher threads: if queue age > X for > Y seconds, auto-dump stacks and attempt thread restart.
- Implement safe on-disk KV compaction with temp files and atomic rename.
- Add runtime flag to auto-fallback to unbatched path when continuous batching latency exceeds threshold.
- Improve observability: specific log markers for "eviction-start/eviction-complete" and counters for "index-repairs".

Communication templates (slack/incident channel):
- Initial post: "Investigating elevated latency for serving-runtime in us-west-2. Symptoms: X% pods showing stalled token gen and increased 5xx. Triage in progress; will update in 15m. On-call: @aisha, @marco."
- Update once mitigation in place: "Mitigation applied: disabled continuous batching on canary pods; QPS recovering to baseline. Collecting traces for postmortem."

Open questions / notes-to-self (unresolved):
- Is there an easy way to snapshot KV cache atomically for offline integrity checks without triggering rebuild? (ask eng-storage)
- Does the runtime expose a safe signal to restart only the batcher loop? If not, add engineering task SR-2471.
- Investigate jemalloc arena fragmentation under 1.9.x runtime build; consider migrating to mimalloc in a follow-up experiment.

Owners and follow-ups (short):
- Incident lead: Aisha Patel (on-call)
- Engineering follow-up: Marco Ruiz (kvcache/eviction) — create PR for checksum improvements
- Batching improvements: Lina Zhao — prototype watchdog and fallback
- Postmortem writeup: Evan Brooks — first draft in 72h, include timeline and RCA

Attachments & artifacts: (place links in linked_artifacts above). Save all raw artifacts under S3: s3://incidents/serving-runtime/playbooks/<<incident-id>>/

Appendix — handy commands (copy-paste):
- Save logs: kubectl logs -n redwood-serving <pod> --since=2h > /tmp/<pod>-logs.txt
- Thread dump via signal: kubectl exec -n redwood-serving <pod> -- kill -SIGUSR1 1
- Heap/stat snapshot: kubectl exec -n redwood-serving <pod> -- cat /var/run/serving/jemalloc_stats > /tmp/<pod>-jemalloc.txt
- KV-checksum: kubectl exec -n redwood-serving <pod> -- /opt/serving/bin/kvcache-checksum --verify-index > /tmp/<pod>-kvcache-checksum.txt
- Controlled restart: kubectl rollout restart deployment/serving-runtime --namespace=redwood-serving --record

Final note: this is intentionally terse and informal — add concrete reproducible testcases as we reproduce in staging and then convert the critical steps into a polished runbook page in Confluence.

Revision log:
- 2025-09-11: Drafted initial playbook (Aisha).
- 2025-09-25: Added KV checksum commands and restart guidance (Marco).
- 2025-10-02: Added batching watchdog idea and owners (Lina).
